archetype.name: Lottery Team (shooting slump)
archetype.definition: A team that won 44 games a year ago and still has the shape of that team, a three-heavy, glass-crashing group, but whose jumper has fallen off a cliff badly enough that it is playing like one of the league's worst sides for now.

report.headline: Last year's shape, none of last year's shooting, and two starters out
report.take:
Charlotte is not a rebuilt team so much as a broken version of last season's. The style is the same, only louder. Last year's Hornets won 44 games with the league's No. 5 offense, an ORtg of 119.4, a 48.7 3PA Rate and strong rebounding at both ends. This year's group takes even more threes, a league-high 51.4 3PA Rate, and rebounds even better, third in ORB % and second in DRB %. The difference is that the shots stopped falling. 3P % has dropped from 37.8 to 28.8, 29th in the league, and with half the attempts coming from deep, that alone takes the offense from fifth to dead last at a 101 ORtg.

The shooting has dragged on everything else. eFG % (46.7) and TS % (50.8) are both 30th. The offense also has nothing to fall back on: FT Rate is 29th, and Charlotte has never been a team that lives at the line in any recent season. Then there is a new problem, ball security. TOV % is 16.8, worst in the league and well above last year's 13.5. Put those together and you get 96.3 points a game, 17 below the league average. The defense is only slightly worse than last year, a 115.6 DRtg against 114.4. Even that number is inflated by opponents hitting 40.8% from three, worst in the league, while the rim defense sits a respectable 12th.

The 3-7 record is, if anything, flattering. The margin implies one win, and W vs Pt Diff is +2, the top luck figure in the league. The trend is worse than the season line: an 0-5 last five at -20.6 a game, inside a six-game losing streak, with blowouts by ATL, DET and BOS. The roster explains some of it. Brandon Miller has carried a 33.2 USG % on 46.5 TS %, so he has been part of the problem rather than the fix, and he is now out along with Dennis Schröder (46.7 TS %, -8.8 BPM). Grayson Allen is the lone efficient creator, at 68 TS % with 32 threes. Behind him the backcourt grade is an F, and the frontcourt rotation of Naz Reid, Moussa Diabaté and Ryan Kalkbrenner has posted wildly different on-off numbers that are mostly small-sample noise.

Our position: the shooting will come back toward normal, both Charlotte's and its opponents'. That makes this closer to a bad-but-not-historic team than the -14.6 Net Rtg suggests. But the turnovers are new, the injuries remove volume, and the luck already banked will give some back. A climb back to .500 looks unlikely this year. A finish in the high 20s to mid 30s in wins is the realistic band.

strengths.title: Owning the glass at both ends
strengths.body: Charlotte grabs 31.8% of its own misses, third in the league, and 76.7% of the opponent's, second. This is a real identity rather than a fluke: last year's team posted a 30.5 ORB % and a 54.0 REB %. With a center rotation of Reid, Diabaté and Kalkbrenner, it should hold up. It is the one thing keeping a 28.8% three-point team within shouting distance on most nights.

strengths.title: Grayson Allen's efficient shooting
strengths.body: Allen is the only high-minute player shooting like last year's offense: a 68 TS %, 141 points and a team-high 32 threes on 20.6 USG %. With Miller and Schröder out, more of the possessions should flow through him. The question is whether that efficiency survives more defensive attention. Some regression from 68 is likely, but he is the template for what this shot profile can look like.

strengths.title: Interior defense is holding
strengths.body: Opponents shoot 63.3% at the rim, 12th in the league and below the league's 65.2. That is about where Charlotte was last year. The defensive damage is coming from the perimeter, where a 40.8 opponent 3P % is far out of line with last year's 35.9. Much of that should fade with more games.

concerns.title: A three-point offense without threes
concerns.body: Charlotte takes a league-high share of its shots from deep and makes only 28.8% of them, against 37.8% last season. With no free-throw game behind it (FT Rate 29th), the whole offense rises and falls on the jumper, and right now it sits 30th at a 101 ORtg. Some bounce-back is near-certain over 72 games. But the main shooters in the sheet besides Allen, Miller at 46.5 TS % and Reid at 50.6, are not yet showing it.

concerns.title: Turnovers are a new leak
concerns.body: A 16.8 TOV % is worst in the league and a sharp break from this franchise's recent seasons, all of which were at or below 13.7. Combined with poor shooting, that means too many empty trips. Losing two ball-handlers to injury does not obviously help, and Christian Anderson Jr. has a -11.6 BPM in his backup minutes.

concerns.title: The record is ahead of the margin
concerns.body: A -139 point differential implies one win, not three, and W vs Pt Diff of +2 ranks first in the league. The last five games have been the worst of the season: 0-5 at -20.6 a game. This is not a team unlucky in close games. If anything, the luck has run its way, and the losing streak reflects how it is actually playing.

trend.note: A 3-4 October with a few competitive wins over BKN, MIA and WSH gave way to an 0-3 November and a six-game skid. The scoring average has fallen to 91.67 a game this month, and the losses have been lopsided.

weekAhead.headline: Cleveland at home, then two shaky West teams on the road
weekAhead.body:
The week opens with the toughest game: Cleveland at home, a 5-5 side ranked 12th on the site, with an A- frontcourt and a top-five defense by Opp eFG %. The one opening is that the Cavaliers force almost nothing, with an Opp TOV % of 11.3 ranked 29th. That is the kindest possible matchup for Charlotte's worst habit. Even so, a shorthanded team shooting this poorly against a solid defense is a lot to ask.

The two road games are where wins are available. Phoenix rebounds worse than anyone, last in DRB % and RPG, and its 120.2 DRtg ranks 27th. That is a perfect setup for Charlotte's offensive rebounding to manufacture second shots. The Clippers are 2-7, turn it over almost as much as Charlotte, and give up big games to shooting guards. Splitting those two would count as a decent week. Going 0-3 would extend the streak to nine and confirm the slide.

keyMatchups.title: Offensive glass versus Phoenix
keyMatchups.body: Phoenix grabs only 65.8% of its defensive rebounds, worst in the league, and allows 25 points a game to centers, 29th. Charlotte's third-ranked ORB % and its center rotation should produce extra possessions. That is the best way for a cold-shooting team to score without making threes.

keyMatchups.title: Allen against the Clippers' guards
keyMatchups.body: The Clippers allow 32.33 points a game to shooting guards, 29th, and 6.79 PRA over those players' usual production, the worst in the league. With Miller out, Allen should get the volume to exploit it. That matchup is likely Charlotte's best shot at a road win.

keyMatchups.title: Cleveland's frontcourt on the boards
keyMatchups.body: Cleveland's frontcourt grades A- and the Cavaliers are fifth in RPG, so the one area where Charlotte reliably wins will be contested. Cleveland's low Opp TOV % gives the Hornets a chance to clean up their giveaways. Without a rebounding edge, though, they will need a shooting night they haven't had lately.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the three-point percentage moves at all with Miller out and Allen taking more of the shots. A couple of nights in the mid-30s would change how this team looks fast.

restOfSeason.body:
Most of what has gone wrong should partially correct. A team that shot 37.8% from three a year ago is unlikely to stay below 29% over 72 more games, and opponents will not keep hitting 40.8% against a defense that is otherwise mid-pack. The rebounding edge is real and repeatable. So the offense should crawl back from 101 toward something like 108 to 113 points per 100, and the Net Rtg should land far closer to last year's bottom-tier teams than to its current -14.6.

The counterweights are real too. The turnover rate is a new and serious problem. Two rotation guards and the team's top scorer are out for an unknown stretch. The +2 W vs Pt Diff will likely give some wins back. The 25-win pace overstates how bad this team is. Our expectation is roughly 27 to 36 wins, well short of last season's 44 unless the shooting returns in full and soon.
swingFactors: How fast the three-point shooting normalizes
Whether the turnover rate falls back toward last year's

confidence.note: Ten games, extreme shooting outliers both ways, and two key players out.
